spans.s: Yukta in the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa (vi. 7, 4, 8; xii. 4, 1, 2) denotes a ‘yoke’ of oxen.

Yuktāśva is the name of a man who is mentioned in the pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa as the seer of a sāman, or chant. He is said to have exposed a pair of twins, but Hopkins thinks that the reference is only to an exchange of children.
Foot notes xi. 8, 8.
Cf. Weber, Naxatra, 2, 314, n., whose view is that of Sāyaṇa on the passage. Cf. yama.
Transactions of the Connecticut Academy of Arts and Sciences, 15, 61, 62.
Cf. Hillebrandt, Vedische
